notes: PHASE-000 foundation is complete and PHASE-001 development is active. WU-002 remains in progress and its acceptance criterion is not yet satisfied because approved desktop calling applications have not consumed processed/bypass audio through an OS-visible VSN virtual microphone. The verified Windows foundation includes Rust audio contracts and bounded queues, deterministic device selection/reselection, bounded stream recovery, IAudioClient3 shared-mode period planning, SharedCapturePlan cadence, event-driven WASAPI capture, native sample decoding/reframing, CaptureRuntime bounded reopen recovery, IMMNotificationClient delivery, bounded virtual-mic staging/output, a versioned Rust protocol, an MSVC x64 C++ ABI mirror, aligned Interlocked cursor publication/stable snapshots and deterministic overflow-safe shared-region geometry. The user-mode transport boundary now creates a real unnamed page-backed Windows file mapping with CreateFileMappingW/MapViewOfFile, derives its size from the validated region layout, enforces a configurable 16 MiB default hard cap, initializes protocol/cursors, disables handle inheritance, and applies a protected DACL containing only LocalSystem full control plus current authenticated process-user read/write access. Windows CI verifies a second independent view observes shared protocol/audio bytes and cursor publication. This shared-section slice passed AI Native Quality Gates run 34536268804 and Windows Audio Validation run 34536269060 on implementation head f38dab24018d1c3b04008675c5ddc36e7520c07b and merged to main as 9f24e8b56c56505df3b736e3fcf3d88ac236c465. A subsequent device-control ABI slice defines versioned CONNECT/DISCONNECT/QUERY_STATUS IOCTL contracts using METHOD_BUFFERED and FILE_READ_ACCESS|FILE_WRITE_ACCESS, locks structure size/alignment/offsets, validates section-handle metadata, mapping size, session generation and expected transport protocol identity, and validates returned runtime status/cursor ordering. Its test constructs CONNECT metadata from a real SharedSection handle but does not issue DeviceIoControl because no VSN WDK device exists yet. That slice passed AI Native Quality Gates run 34536677479 and Windows Audio Validation run 34536677410 on implementation head 8a14b010d0c6b3e097e67d4488194734c2c0142e and merged to main as a5a372ac819d2fe2e76f6cbedc54e62bc05d4ec6. These results prove a real user-mode section and a driver-facing control ABI, not a kernel consumer or OS-visible microphone. Still pending are kernel-side caller authorization and section-handle referencing/mapping, secure device-interface ACL/IOCTL dispatch, WDK WaveRT endpoint/topology/buffering/position behavior, physical hotplug/default-device recovery on controlled hardware, hardware CPU/latency/jitter/deadline targets, processed/bypass audio reaching approved calling applications, and driver signing/install/update/uninstall/rollback. The next valid WU-002 action is to establish the WDK-buildable virtual-mic driver/control skeleton and implement the kernel-side CONNECT validation/reference lifecycle against the verified device-control and shared-region contracts, while continuing to avoid any OS-visible endpoint claim until driver build/install/runtime evidence exists. Paid provider usage, proprietary model training, production credentials/cloud spend and production deployment remain subject to applicable provider/data/compute/release gates.
